title: Demonstrative adjectives
goal: By the end of this lesson you can point things out with ce, cet, cette and ces, choose the right form before a vowel, and use -ci and -là to contrast 'this one here' and 'that one there'.

learn.h: Four forms: ce, cet, cette, ces
body: Demonstrative adjectives mean 'this', 'that', 'these' or 'those'. They replace the article and agree with the noun: **ce** *livre*, **cette** *maison*, **ces** *enfants*.
French does not usually distinguish 'this' and 'that': *ce film* can mean this movie or that movie. Context decides.

head: Singular
Plural
rows: ce (cet before a vowel / silent h)
ce chien, cet ami, cet hôtel, cette rue

learn.tip: Cet and cette sound the same: [sèt]. Only spelling tells them apart.

learn.h: Cet: the masculine before a vowel
body: Before a masculine noun starting with a vowel or a silent *h*, *ce* becomes **cet** so the words link smoothly: *cet arbre*, *cet homme*, *cet hiver*, *cet été*.
This also applies when an adjective comes first: *cet autre livre*, *cet ancien collègue*. And with *ces*, make the liaison in [z]: *ces‿enfants*, *ces‿hôtels*.
Demonstratives are everywhere in time expressions: *ce matin* (this morning), *cet après-midi*, *ce soir* (tonight), *cette semaine*, *ce week-end / cette fin de semaine*, *cet été*, *cette année*.
To say 'that' time in the past, add *-là*: *ce jour-là* (that day), *cette année-là* (that year), *à ce moment-là* (at that moment).

learn.h: This one vs that one: -ci and -là
body: To contrast two things, attach **-ci** (here, closer) or **-là** (there, farther) to the noun with a hyphen: *Je préfère* **cette robe-ci**, *pas* **cette robe-là**.
In everyday speech *-là* is far more common than *-ci*, and it often just adds emphasis: *Ce gars-là est vraiment gentil.* (That guy is really nice.)

examples.fr: Cette rue est toujours en construction.
examples.en: This street is always under construction.

examples.fr: Cet hôtel est près du Vieux-Port.
examples.en: This hotel is near the Old Port.

examples.fr: Ces bottes sont parfaites pour l'hiver.
examples.en: These boots are perfect for winter.

examples.fr: Qu'est-ce que tu fais ce soir?
Cet été, on va en Gaspésie.
examples.en: This summer, we're going to the Gaspé.
That day, it was snowing a lot.

examples.fr: Ces enfants jouent dehors tous les jours.
examples.en: Those children play outside every day.

examples.fr: Cette fin de semaine, il va faire beau.
examples.en: This weekend, the weather is going to be nice.

examples.fr: C'est ce livre-là que je cherchais!
examples.en: That's the book I was looking for!

quebec.intro: In Quebec speech, ce and cette are often squeezed into 'c'te' (said [st]), and almost every demonstrative gets a '-là' tag: 'c'te gars-là', 'c'te femme-là'. The -là tag even attaches to nouns with le or la: 'le gars-là'. Write the standard forms.

items.en: This year, I'm working a lot.

items.note: à soir / à matin = ce soir / ce matin; informal
-là on a definite noun; malade = awesome (slang)

drills.why: Arbre is masculine and starts with a vowel: cet.
Hiver is masculine with a silent h: cet.
Masculine before a vowel: cet; feminine: cette.
Après-midi is masculine and starts with a vowel: cet.
-là for a time in the past.
Gâteau is masculine and starts with a consonant: ce.

drills.en: What are you doing this weekend?
drills.a: Qu'est-ce que tu fais cette fin de semaine?

drills.en: That year, we lived in Laval.
a: Cette année-là, nous habitions à Laval.
Cette année-là, on habitait à Laval.
Cette année-là, nous vivions à Laval.
Cette année-là, on vivait à Laval.
drills.why: Cette année-là + imparfait for a past situation.

pron.tip: [suh] vs [sé]: the vowel tells you singular or plural.
Both [sèt]. You can't hear the difference.
Quebec: [st' gâ la], the â is long and back.
Quebec: [a swar], sometimes [a swèr] in rural speech.

dialogue.fr: Bonjour! Je cherche des bottes pour l'hiver.
dialogue.en: Hello! I'm looking for winter boots.

dialogue.fr: Ces bottes-ci sont très chaudes. Elles sont bonnes jusqu'à moins quarante.
dialogue.en: These boots here are very warm. They're good to minus forty.
And those boots, next to them?

dialogue.fr: Elles sont plus belles, mais moins chaudes.
dialogue.en: They're nicer, but not as warm.

dialogue.fr: Hmm. Cet hiver, je vais beaucoup marcher. Je prends ces bottes-ci.
dialogue.en: Hmm. This winter, I'm going to walk a lot. I'll take these boots.

dialogue.fr: Bon choix! Vous voulez aussi cette tuque-là? Elle est en solde.
dialogue.en: Good choice! Would you also like that toque? It's on sale.

dialogue.fr: Ah oui, c'te tuque-là est vraiment belle. Je la prends!
dialogue.en: Oh yes, that toque is really nice. I'll take it!

questions.q: Why does A choose the first pair of boots?
What does A plan to do this winter?

speak.prompt: Look around the room and point out 4 objects with ce, cet, cette and ces.
speak.model: Ce téléphone est vieux. Cet ordinateur est lent. Cette lampe est belle. Ces livres sont à moi.

speak.prompt: You're shopping. Compare two items with -ci and -là and choose one.
speak.model: Ce manteau-ci est chaud, mais ce manteau-là est plus beau. Je prends ce manteau-là!

speak.prompt: Say 'That guy is funny' and 'Tonight we're going out' in standard French, then Quebec style.
speak.model: Ce gars est drôle. Ce soir, on sort. / C'te gars-là est drôle. À soir, on sort.

write.prompt: Write 5–6 sentences about your plans and things around you, using at least five demonstratives (including one cet, one time expression, and one -là).
write.model: Cette semaine, je suis très occupé. Ce matin, j'ai travaillé à la maison. Cet après-midi, je vais au gym. Ce soir, je soupe avec des amis dans ce nouveau restaurant libanais. Cette fin de semaine, je vais me reposer. Ces vacances-là, je les attends depuis longtemps!

quiz.why: Feminine: always cette, even before a vowel.
Homme is masculine with silent h: cet.

quiz.q: What is the plural of 'cette idée'?
'À soir' is the spoken Quebec form of…
quiz.why: On sort à soir = on sort ce soir.
